To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is a large range of hip fracture probabilities in different countries, and that these probabilities can be used for adjusting intervention thresholds.

there is a 15‐ to 20‐fold range in the 10‐year hip fracture probability between countries and that there are significant correlations of 1) hip fracture probability and mortality between men and women in the same country and 2) hip fracture probability between men and women from different countries.
there is a large heterogeneity in hip fracture probability in men and women across different countries, which can be used to develop intervention thresholds for different countries.

the development of a new approach for the prevention of hip fracture.
the development of a new method of risk assessment for hip fractures.
the development and evaluation of a new method of assessing hip fracture probability in the elderly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a large heterogeneity of hip fractures from different regions of world and the intervention threshold for the hip fracture should be based on the age, sex, relative risk, and absolute risk.
there is a large heterogeneity of hip fractures across the globe.
the risk of hip fracture is highly variable between different populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hip fracture risk is very high in the Scandinavian countries, high in the United States and other European and Asian countries, medium in some countries, and very low in some countries.
hip fracture probability is a strong predictor of hip fracture incidence.
the probability of fracture in a given population is the product of the incidence and survival rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hip fracture risk varies widely between countries and regions of the world, and that these differences can be used to estimate hip fracture risk in different populations.

there is a large heterogeneity of hip fractures in different regions of the globe and that this heterogeneity is associated with differences in mortality and that these factors need to be considered when developing intervention thresholds.

there is a wide variation in the probability of hip fractures across the world and this variation needs to be taken into account in the development of risk assessment tools and in the development of guidelines for intervention thresholds.
